subject.title: feat(github-copilot): support GitHub Enterprise data-residency Copilot auth

question: Should OpenClaw accept this bounded `github-copilot` auth/config boundary for GitHub Enterprise data-residency tenants?
rationale: The patch is technically sound and well proven, but it intentionally changes where token-bearing Copilot auth/runtime requests may go and adds provider-owned config/env/auth-method surface that automation should not approve as product/security policy on its own.

options.title: Accept provider-owned tenant routing
options.body: Land the PR as the supported fix for `*.ghe.com` data-residency Copilot users, with the current allowlist, domain-scoped cache, guided auth choice, and env/config override.

options.title: Narrow to config-only routing
options.body: Ask for a follow-up revision that keeps tenant host routing but removes or defers the interactive `device-enterprise` surface and SDK export expansion.

options.title: Reject bundled-provider routing
options.body: Close or pause this PR and keep the work in a different provider/plugin/API direction despite the live proof.

recommendation.title: Accept provider-owned tenant routing
recommendation.body: Land the PR as the supported fix for `*.ghe.com` data-residency Copilot users, with the current allowlist, domain-scoped cache, guided auth choice, and env/config override.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle is tied to current source history, listed security/agent ownership, and cited owner guidance on this PR.
